items.stem: ‘The Union won the Civil War mainly because of its greater economic resources.’ Discuss.
items.answer: For: The Union had far more industry, railways and money. Its larger population allowed it to replace losses. The blockade and economic strength wore down the South. Against: Union leadership, especially Lincoln and Grant, was vital. Confederate weaknesses, such as states' rights disputes and inflation, undermined its war effort. Key victories such as Gettysburg, Vicksburg and Atlanta were not inevitable. Emancipation and Black soldiers strengthened the Union. Judgement: resources gave the Union a decisive advantage in a long war, but it took effective leadership and military victories to convert them into victory.

items.stem: ‘Radical Reconstruction transformed the position of African Americans in the South.’ Discuss.
items.answer: For: The Fourteenth and Fifteenth Amendments gave citizenship and the vote. Hundreds of African Americans held office. Schools, churches and families were built or reunited with Freedmen's Bureau support. Against: Most remained landless sharecroppers. Violence by the Klan and others limited freedom. The gains were reversed after 1877. Judgement: Radical Reconstruction brought revolutionary legal and political change, but without economic independence it did not transform daily life for most freed people.

items.stem: What is meant by “contrabands”?
options: Enslaved people who escaped to Union lines, treated as captured enemy property from 1861.
Lincoln's early proposal that states free enslaved people over time with payment to owners.
Fast ships that tried to evade the Union naval blockade of southern ports.
The members of the Republican Party who pressed for immediate emancipation and equal rights.
items.answer: Enslaved people who escaped to Union lines, treated as captured enemy property from 1861.
items.markingKey: Contrabands: enslaved people who escaped to Union lines, treated as captured enemy property from 1861. [1]

items.stem: Explain why Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation.
items.answer: It weakened the Confederacy by attacking its labour force. It allowed the recruitment of Black soldiers. It made foreign intervention on the side of the South less likely. Enslaved people escaping to Union lines had already undermined slavery. Lincoln had come to see emancipation as a moral and political necessity. Judgement: it was presented as a military measure, which made it constitutional, but it reflected a political and moral shift.

items.stem: Tariq is planning an answer to the question: “‘Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation mainly as a military measure.’ How far do you agree?” Write a one-sentence line of argument for the answer and outline two points Tariq could use to support the view and two to challenge it.
items.answer: Line of argument: it was framed as a military measure for constitutional reasons, but it reflected moral conviction and political pressure as much as military need. Support: It was justified as a war measure under his powers as commander-in-chief. It applied only to areas in rebellion, where it would damage the enemy. Challenge: Lincoln had long opposed slavery morally. Pressure from Radicals, abolitionists and Black leaders shaped the decision.
items.markingKey: 2 marks for a line of argument that answers the question directly and is sustainable; 1 mark for each relevant supporting point and 1 for each challenging point [6]

items.stem: Which of these events happened first?
options: Lincoln announced the Ten Percent Plan
The first Reconstruction Act was passed
items.answer: Lincoln announced the Ten Percent Plan
items.markingKey: Lincoln announced the Ten Percent Plan (December 1863); the first Reconstruction Act was passed (March 1867); Andrew Johnson was impeached (February 1868); the Fifteenth Amendment was ratified (February 1870). [1]

items.stem: The Reconstruction Acts of 1867 divided the former Confederacy into five military districts. Explain why Congress took control of Reconstruction from President Johnson in 1866-67.
items.answer: Johnson's lenient terms allowed former Confederates back into power. Southern states passed Black Codes. Violence such as the Memphis and New Orleans riots of 1866 shocked the North. Johnson vetoed the Freedmen's Bureau and Civil Rights bills. Republicans won large majorities in the 1866 elections. Judgement: the South's defiance under Johnson's plan persuaded northern voters that stronger federal action was needed.

items.stem: Historians have offered several reasons why Radical Reconstruction achieved only limited change for African Americans. A: Northern commitment to racial equality was shallow. B: Most freed people did not get land and became sharecroppers. C: Federal enforcement was limited and declined after 1872. Which was the most significant? Explain your answer with reference to the other reasons.
items.answer: Any reasoned choice. A: Northern commitment to racial equality was shallow. B: Most freed people did not get land and became sharecroppers. C: Federal enforcement was limited and declined after 1872. Possible judgement: without land or lasting federal protection, the political gains of Radical Reconstruction were vulnerable.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for a choice; up to 3 marks for explaining it with precise detail; up to 2 marks for comparing it with the other reasons [6]

items.stem: How far was Andrew Johnson responsible for the failure of Presidential Reconstruction?
items.answer: For: He pardoned many former Confederates. He tolerated the Black Codes. He vetoed civil rights legislation and alienated moderate Republicans. Against: White southerners resisted any change to racial hierarchy. Lincoln's lenient plan had set the pattern. Congress was divided on how far to go. Judgement: Johnson's policies and stubbornness made the failure worse, but southern white resistance was the underlying cause.

Level 4 (15-17): developed analysis of both sides; a judgement is reached but is not fully supported. Level 3 (10-14): analysis of one side, or of both with limited development or accuracy. Level 2 (6-9): mainly descriptive, with implicit links to the question. Level 1 (1-5): general assertions with little accurate knowledge. Agree / supporting: He pardoned many former Confederates. He tolerated the Black Codes. He vetoed civil rights legislation and alienated moderate Republicans. Disagree / other factors: White southerners resisted any change to racial hierarchy. Lincoln's lenient plan had set the pattern. Congress was divided on how far to go. Possible judgement: Johnson's policies and stubbornness made the failure worse, but southern white resistance was the underlying cause. [20]

items.stem: Put these events in chronological order, starting with the earliest. A: The Ku Klux Klan Act was passed. B: Democrats used the Mississippi Plan to win state elections. C: Federal troops were withdrawn from the last southern state capitals. D: The Panic of 1873 began.
items.markingKey: Correct order A, D, B, C (A 1871; D 1873; B 1875; C April 1877): 2 marks if all correct, 1 mark if one adjacent pair is reversed. [2]

items.stem: A revision guide lists these reasons why African Americans lost many of the rights gained during Reconstruction after 1877. A: Southern states introduced poll taxes and literacy tests. B: Violence and lynching went unpunished. C: Segregation laws spread. Explain which of these was the most important reason.
items.answer: Any reasoned choice. A: Southern states introduced poll taxes and literacy tests. B: Violence and lynching went unpunished. C: Segregation laws spread. Possible judgement: once federal protection was withdrawn, southern states could remove rights by law and force.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for a choice; up to 3 marks for explaining it with precise detail; up to 2 marks for comparing it with the other reasons [6]

items.stem: Consider the following explanations of why African Americans lost many of the rights gained during Reconstruction after 1877. A: Segregation laws spread. Explain your answer with reference to the other reasons.
items.answer: Any reasoned choice. A: Segregation laws spread. B: Violence and lynching went unpunished. C: The Supreme Court allowed segregation in Plessy v. Ferguson (1896). Possible judgement: once federal protection was withdrawn, southern states could remove rights by law and force.

items.stem: Name the term that matches this description: “the Confederate belief that Britain and France would intervene to secure cotton supplies”.
items.answer: King Cotton diplomacy

items.stem: Which of these statements is accurate?
options: Lee invaded the North twice, at Antietam and at Gettysburg.
Freed people were given forty acres of land each by Congress.
The Compromise of 1877 was a formal treaty approved by Congress.
The Union blockade was completely effective from 1861.
items.answer: Lee invaded the North twice, at Antietam and at Gettysburg.
items.markingKey: Both invasions ended in retreat. The other statements are inaccurate. [1]

items.stem: Mei is planning an answer to the question: “‘The Union won the Civil War mainly because of its greater economic resources.’ How far do you agree?” Write a one-sentence line of argument for the answer and outline two points Mei could use to support the view and two to challenge it.
items.answer: Line of argument: resources gave the Union a decisive advantage in a long war, but it took effective leadership and military victories to convert them into victory. Support: The Union had far more industry, railways and money. Its larger population allowed it to replace losses. Challenge: Union leadership, especially Lincoln and Grant, was vital. Confederate weaknesses, such as states' rights disputes and inflation, undermined its war effort.
items.markingKey: 2 marks for a line of argument that answers the question directly and is sustainable; 1 mark for each relevant supporting point and 1 for each challenging point [6]

items.stem: What is meant by “Confiscation Acts”?
options: A war won by wearing down the enemy's resources and manpower.
Northern Democrats who opposed the war and wanted a negotiated peace.
Laws of 1861 and 1862 allowing Union forces to seize property, including enslaved people, used to support the rebellion.
The informal agreement by which Hayes became president and federal troops were withdrawn from the South.
items.answer: Laws of 1861 and 1862 allowing Union forces to seize property, including enslaved people, used to support the rebellion.
items.markingKey: Confiscation Acts: laws of 1861 and 1862 allowing Union forces to seize property, including enslaved people, used to support the rebellion. [1]

items.stem: The Thirteenth Amendment, abolishing slavery throughout the United States, was ratified in December 1865. Explain why slavery collapsed in the South during the war.
items.answer: Enslaved people fled to Union lines in large numbers. Union armies freed people as they advanced. The Confiscation Acts and the Proclamation gave legal backing. Black soldiers fought for freedom. The Thirteenth Amendment made abolition permanent. Judgement: slavery was destroyed by the actions of enslaved people and Union armies, then made permanent by law.

items.stem: Leila is planning an answer to the question: “To what extent did enslaved people free themselves during the Civil War?” Write a one-sentence line of argument for the answer and outline two points Leila could use to support the view and two to challenge it.
items.answer: Line of argument: enslaved people played a central role in destroying slavery, but their freedom depended on Union victory and federal law. Support: Hundreds of thousands fled to Union lines. Escapes forced Union commanders and Congress to act. Challenge: Union armies were needed to make freedom real. The Proclamation and Thirteenth Amendment provided legal freedom.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements is correct?

The Union blockade was completely effective from 1861.
African Americans held public office in the South during Reconstruction.

items.stem: Zara is planning an answer to the question: “‘Radical Reconstruction transformed the position of African Americans in the South.’ How far do you agree?” Write a one-sentence line of argument for the answer and outline two points Zara could use to support the view and two to challenge it.
items.answer: Line of argument: Radical Reconstruction brought revolutionary legal and political change, but without economic independence it did not transform daily life for most freed people. Support: The Fourteenth and Fifteenth Amendments gave citizenship and the vote. Hundreds of African Americans held office. Challenge: Most remained landless sharecroppers. Violence by the Klan and others limited freedom.
items.markingKey: 2 marks for a line of argument that answers the question directly and is sustainable; 1 mark for each relevant supporting point and 1 for each challenging point [6]

items.stem: Read the sources carefully. Source A: a letter from a Freedmen's Bureau agent in Georgia, 1868 (illustrative). “The freedmen have voted and some now sit in the legislature, but on the plantations little has changed. Without land they must work on whatever terms the planter offers, and the night riders punish any who resist.” Source B: a speech by a Black member of a southern state legislature, 1868 (illustrative). “Three years ago we were slaves; today we make laws. We have built schools in every county and we shall not go back.” How far do Sources A and B support the view that Radical Reconstruction transformed the position of African Americans in the South?
items.answer: Source A challenges: it shows the limits of change in daily life. Evaluation: agents had reasons to stress problems to secure more support. Source B supports: it shows political and educational transformation. Evaluation: it is a political speech intended to inspire. Grouping: support B; challenge A. A judgement must weigh how convincing each group is, using provenance and own knowledge, rather than counting sources.

Level 4 (13-16): uses the sources to support AND challenge the view and evaluates some of them. Level 3 (9-12): uses the sources at face value to support AND challenge. Level 2 (5-8): uses the sources to support OR challenge. Level 1 (1-4): writes about the topic without valid use of the sources. items.stem: Tomás is planning an answer to the question: “‘Reconstruction ended mainly because the North lost interest.’ How far do you agree?” Write a one-sentence line of argument for the answer and outline two points Tomás could use to support the view and two to challenge it.
items.answer: Line of argument: southern violence destroyed Reconstruction state by state, but it could succeed only because the North was no longer willing to intervene. Support: The depression after 1873 turned attention to economic issues. Democrats won the House in 1874. Challenge: White southern violence and intimidation overthrew Republican governments. Supreme Court decisions limited federal power.
